exceptions.name: dependency-cruiser
exceptions.rationale: Invoked by scripts/dep-cruise.cjs via spawnSync against the resolved node_modules/dependency-cruiser/bin/dependency-cruise.mjs binary path, never through a JS import/require('dependency-cruiser') statement — knip's dependency-usage graph can only trace the latter.

exceptions.name: next
exceptions.rationale: tsconfig.nextjs.json's `compilerOptions.plugins: [{ name: "next" }]` is a TypeScript-language-service plugin declaration (editor/tsc IntelliSense only), not a runtime import — knip's unresolved-import check misreads the plugin `name` field as a module specifier. packages/config has no dependency on next itself; the real consumer (apps/web) already declares it.
Notification delivery failures are consumed by asynchronous event handlers and have no HTTP transport mapper.

notification is fully event-driven and has no contexts/notification/infrastructure/http/notification-error.mapper.ts at all — same reasoning as the EmailDeliveryException error-mapper-coverage exception above: notification-log.aggregate.ts (this path) constructs Email, but any validation failure there is handled by the async event-handler flow, never an HTTP transport mapper.
Legacy availability adapter requires a repository-port follow-up before Story 2 enforcement.

This IS the centralized same-origin gateway Route Handler — it forwards arbitrary requests, cookies, redirects, and response headers to the BFF. The sanctioned transport helpers are for feature code calling through the gateway, not the gateway's own implementation.

Calls this app's own /api/auth/** and /api/customers/tenants Route Handlers (same-origin, not the BFF/backend directly) — each Route Handler itself uses bffServerFetch (TD31 Story 7 pattern, 2026-07-31).
Calls this app's own /api/customers/me Route Handler (same-origin, not the BFF/backend directly) — the Route Handler itself uses bffServerFetch (TD31 Story 7 pattern, 2026-07-31).
Calls this app's own /api/staff/me Route Handler (same-origin, not the BFF/backend directly) — the Route Handler itself uses bffServerFetch (TD31 Story 7 pattern, 2026-07-31).
Calls this app's own /api/session Route Handler (same-origin, not the BFF/backend directly) — the Route Handler itself uses bffServerFetch (TD31 Story 7 pattern, 2026-07-31).
fetchBookingsViaProxy() calls this app's own /api/bookings Route Handler (same-origin, not the BFF/backend directly) — the Route Handler itself uses bffServerFetch (TD31 Story 7 pattern, 2026-07-31).

createCustomerAttachmentSignedUrl() calls /api/bookings/attachments/signed-url, this app's own Route Handler, not the BFF directly — that route reads the access_token cookie server-side and forwards it as Authorization: Bearer, scoping the request to the authenticated customer's own tenant (TD31 Story 7, 2026-07-31).

submitLeadFormClient() calls /api/platform/lead-form/submissions, this app's own Route Handler, not the BFF directly — that route reads the session cookie server-side and forwards it as Authorization: Bearer for a logged-in customer submission (UC-040), mirroring createCustomerAttachmentSignedUrl()'s exact reasoning (TD31 Story 7 pattern, M20-S09 story-discovery).

createAttachmentSignedUrl()/createGuestAttachmentSignedUrl() call /api/bookings/attachments/signed-url, this app's own Route Handler, not the BFF directly — the route deliberately ignores any leftover cookie when a guestToken is present in the body; routing through bffClient's generic gateway would transparently forward whatever cookie the browser has and risk misattributing the upload (TD31 Story 7, 2026-07-31).
Uploads directly to a GCS/S3 pre-signed URL returned by the BFF — this leg of the flow is not a BFF/backend endpoint, so the transport helpers don't apply.
Calls the public ViaCEP Brazilian postal-code lookup API (viacep.com.br) — an approved third-party service, not the BFF/backend.

TD37-S05: a domain aggregate with many small, cohesive methods naturally exceeds the 250-line file cap even after extracting every type/mapper that could safely move out (booking.types.ts) — splitting Booking's remaining methods across files to satisfy the metric would fragment one cohesive domain concept, not reduce real complexity (max-lines-per-function still applies and is enforced/fixed on this file).

M20-S02: naming-heuristic false positive — the registry's `Address` concept matches any property name ending in the literal suffix 'Address', but LeadFormSubmission.ipAddress is a network IP address (abuse-investigation trail / rate-limit key, VARCHAR(45), docs/13-DATABASE_SCHEMA.md), not a postal address (street/city/state/zipCode). The same real-world concept already exists elsewhere in this codebase as a plain string with no VO — ChatbotSession.clientIp (chatbot-session.aggregate.ts) — which only avoided this same flag because its property name doesn't happen to end in 'Address'.
